questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get better at speaking French.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall amazing, some things at the university were not so good.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. The university's relationship with Erasmus is a little chaotic in some ways, however they are often also very kind to them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A team of young guides that all of us Danes from different classes met personally at Sorbonne University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was mostly when the semester started that everything became very confusing. The help was very good before that.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fondation Danoise for danish students was extremely easy to get into and amazing overall.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing, French students often live with their families until they are around 25. I do not think anyone I knew lived together. As an exchange student, it is good to live with people in some way if possible. It was very hard to make friends at the university itself, you make them by going out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not know if there was housing for students or not, I had Fondation Danoise from early on.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Confusing. Their system of ECTS is difficult, some subjects have maybe 3 points, others have maybe 8, you have to make a puzzle with your calendar, that can be annoying. However it was very easy to get the classes, nothing was denied to me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to find the course descriptions yourself, use a special file to choose them, that the coordinator will give to you, you can change classes very easily after.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the other international students for help, we had a huge group on Whatsapp which was extremely helpful, someone made it after our first meeting together at Sorbonne, it saved me many times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A little bit old school sometimes, some courses were very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but you have to remember things in your head to pass the exams that are in hand and with out any tools for helping.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teacher has more power and authority, which can be a good thing. It is possible to ask questions, but people do not do it all the time. The way to write assignments can be very specific, which you have to ask the teacher how to do.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Littérature et édition + Littérature française classique et moderne + Études comparatistes + Patrimoine culturel français (option FLE) + Techniques et langages des médias

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of those above if you are interested in literature, though the first and second were quite difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Living in Paris is quite expensive, especially groceries, though eating out is cheap, going out can also be quite expensive, clubs are more expensive than at home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport was cheaper than expected, get Navigo Easy with reduced rate, not the monthly card, or bike through Velib or Swapfiet.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Zero activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They were not any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hang out at the school, sit in the courtyard or sit at the library, sometimes people will talk to you, you could talk to them, but overall nothing really happens otherwise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go drinking and talk to people there, it is much easier. Go to the rest of France, it is so beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The school was quite different, but nothing was too dramatically different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just ask them practical questions, maybe they will open up. It helps a lot with being good at French, practice as much as you can before.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The school was really not supposed to be a fun place to be. No couches to sit on, no bars.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The professionalism of the teachers, the ambition of some of the courses.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Practice your speaking and listening skills as much as you, do not worry about reading and writing. Make a chat group with the international students, you can help each other. Be careful with choosing courses in the 3rd year since they can be difficult, but do it if you really want to learn something, the courses in the 1st year are ridiculously easy, and prepare yourself well for the exams.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can ask the other students for notes, they are often very willing to give them to international students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of being in a French school was super interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding and speaking in French. You do not have to say anything in classes, you can easily escape it, but it is very important to sit in front row and listen well, not all teachers speak clearly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
